sources.title: Antigravity agent | Gemini API | Google AI for Developers
sources.notes: Official Gemini API docs (antigravity agent + managed agents quickstart pages).
sources.text: The antigravity-preview-09-2026 version was released and replaces the previous antigravity-preview-05-2026. You can make a basic API call using curl with the agent set to "antigravity-preview-09-2026", provide input text, and set environment to "remote". You can use the Google GenAI Python client to create an interaction with the agent "antigravity-preview-09-2026", pass input text, and set environment to "remote". Each call can provision a Linux sandbox and starts a tool-use loop where the agent plans, acts, observes results, and repeats until the task is done. The agent can run Bash, Python, and Node.js commands, install packages, run tests, build apps, and read, write, edit, search, and list files in the sandbox. You should store interaction.id and interaction.environment_id to continue the conversation in the same sandbox, use interaction.output_text to access the agent's final response, and interaction.steps lists each step the agent took.

sources.title: Gemini API Managed Agents Update
sources.notes: Google AI Studio's own announcement of the update.
sources.text: Gemini managed agents are getting an updated harness with antigravity-preview-09-2026, which brings the agent's tools and behavior closer to what you get in the Antigravity Coding Agent, and runs on Gemini 3.8 Flash with the model configurable per interaction. Two new APIs make building with managed agents easier and more secure: a Files API for getting data in and out of the agent's environment, and a Credentials API so the agent can use the services you already use, from MCP servers to third-party APIs, in a secure way. Files API: You can upload into a running sandbox, list what the agent wrote, and download the files you need. Credentials API: You can register secrets once and attach them to an MCP server or a sandbox environment variable, and the model never sees them. Bearer tokens, environment variables, and OAuth2 credentials are never visible to the model. Backward Compatibility: Requests that work on antigravity-preview-05-2026 work unchanged on the new harness. However, antigravity-preview-05-2026 will be deprecated on October 5, 2026, after which requests to it are redirected to the updated harness.

sources.title: Introducing Managed Agents in the Gemini API
sources.retrieved_by: WebSearch(allowed_domains=[ai.google.dev, blog.google, developers.googleblog.com]) extract via Claude Code session
sources.notes: Google blog + docs extract (multiple Google pages). Mentions Gemini 3.5 Flash for the original agent; the September update (s2) says 3.8 Flash.
sources.text: Managed Agents in the Gemini API is rolling out in preview in the Gemini API. With a single call, you can spin up an agent that reasons, uses tools and executes code in an isolated, ephemeral Linux environment. The Antigravity agent is built on Gemini 3.5 Flash and available via the Interactions API and in Google AI Studio. Google AI Studio Playground provides a visual interface to prototype and learn how to build managed agents without having to create and write API calls. The Agents tab has a series of templates that pre-configure the base Antigravity Agent by setting tool and environment configurations. Credentials can be passed to managed agents through MCP servers or other tools using a credential parameter. File management allows reading, writing, editing, searching, and listing files in the sandbox, with files persisting across interactions.

sources.title: Google AI Studio introduces Managed Agents in the Gemini API with an updated harness, Files API, and managed credentials — AICoder
sources.retrieved_by: WebSearch(allowed_domains=[aicoder.com]) extract via Claude Code session
sources.notes: Independent coverage. Published date taken from the URL slug (news-20260919).
sources.text: Google AI Studio shared Managed Agents for the Gemini API, adding an updated agent harness, a Files API, and managed credentials. The combination brings long-running agent execution, file context, and credential handling into a managed path instead of forcing developers to assemble each control plane themselves. Updated Agent Harness: The updated agent harness provides a more complete managed runtime for Gemini API agents. Files API: The Files API adds a dedicated file-context surface for agent workflows. Managed Credentials: Managed credentials reduce the operational burden of storing and rotating tool credentials in each app. antigravity-preview-09-2026 is live in the Interactions API and AI Studio, giving agents isolated Linux execution, filesystem tools, web search, persistent environments, and MCP connectivity. It is not a new Pro/Flash model but the Antigravity managed-agent endpoint: Linux sandbox with code execution, files, and browser, defaulting to Gemini 3.8 Flash.

sources.title: Google's Gemini Agent Update: 22% Efficiency Boost, Files API, and Credentials API Live Now
sources.notes: Tech blog. Its free-tier statement is not confirmed by a Google source in this capture.
sources.text: Google rolled out the antigravity-preview-09-2026 harness for Gemini Managed Agents, featuring Gemini 3.8 Flash, a 22% caching boost, Files API, and secure Credentials API. The antigravity-preview-09-2026 harness, along with the Files and Credentials APIs, is available immediately across Google's developer surface areas: Google AI Studio (where developers can prototype agents using a visual interface, configure system prompts, attach datasets via the Files API, and test tool integrations directly) and the Interactions API for production applications. Google has included access to these new harness capabilities within the standard free tier limits in Google AI Studio, allowing teams to test performance.

sources.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 \ Anthropic
sources.text: Claude Fable 5.1 sets a new standard for coding, knowledge work, and long-running problem-solving tasks. It is a Mythos-level model built for your most ambitious, long-running projects that avoids easy-seeming shortcuts, fixes the root causes of problems rather than the symptoms, and keeps you updated as it works. Fable 5.1 defaults to High effort in Claude Code. Fable 5.1 supports a 1 million token context window for long sessions with large codebases. Both models support a 1M token context window by default, 128k max output tokens, and always-on adaptive thinking. When set to Low or Medium effort, Fable 5.1 achieves results similar to or better than Fable 5's at a much lower cost. Claude Fable 5.1 is priced at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, with cache reads now costing $0.25 per million tokens.

sources.title: What to know about the Sora discontinuation | OpenAI Help Center
sources.text: The Sora web and app experiences were discontinued on April 26, 2026. The Sora API will be discontinued on September 24, 2026. You can export your data, and it's recommended you export your Sora content as soon as possible.
